card.title: 5th WILNO BRIGADE
card.text: Deployment: Convert this unit into target unit.
card.flavorText: The 5th Wilno Brigade was part of the 5th Kresowa Infantry Division, a Polish unit formed in 1943 in the Middle East under British command. The division drew its manpower from Polish soldiers who had been released from Soviet labor camps after the Sikorski-Mayski Agreement. Composed mostly of men from Poland's eastern territories, the 5th Kresowa Infantry Division was trained and equipped by the British and became part of the Polish II Corps under General Władysław Anders. It first saw combat in the Italian Campaign, beginning in early 1944. It played a crucial role during the Fourth Battle of Monte Cassino, capturing the strategic Hill 593 while enduring heavy losses. After Cassino, the division continued its advance through Italy, participating in the battles of Ancona and for the Gothic Line. It was known for its determination and resilience despite limited reinforcements. By the end of the war, the 5th Kresowa had suffered over 5,000 casualties. The unit remained in Italy until 1946, then demobilized in the United Kingdom. Many of its soldiers stayed there, whether by choice or not.
